topic: Crows recognize human faces and hold grudges (UW mask study)
hook: Crows remember your face for years
caption:
In 2006, researchers at the University of Washington wore a caveman mask while trapping a few wild crows. Years later, crows on campus still dive-bombed and scolded anyone wearing that mask, even birds that were never caught.

Crows learn faces, share warnings with each other and remember for years. Tomorrow's Part 2 covers what else these birds can do. Follow so you don't miss it.

Have you ever had a bird that seemed to recognise you?

1/4 Crows remember your face for years
In Seattle, scientists in masks trapped crows. Years later, crows still scolded that exact mask.
🎨 AI-generated image

2/4 They pass on the grudge (Shared)
Crows that were never trapped learned to scold the mask too, by copying the others.
📷 Sardaka (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

3/4 They judge the face (Face)
A neutral mask worn on the same walks got almost no scolding. Only the 'dangerous' face mattered.
📷 Alexis Lours (CC BY 4.0) via wikimedia

4/4 Brain scans agree (Fear)
Seeing the threatening face lit up crow brain areas linked to fear and learning, much like ours.
